newsitem.title: FRANCE: French childrens' channel sets 1st TV ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: French childrens' channel sets 1st TV ad campaign.

text.p: Canal J, a French television channel for children available only on cable or satellite networks, said on Friday it is running its first advertising campaign on terrestrial television from August 2 to August 10.
The campaign, devised by advertising agency 20/80, uses a film which already runs on Canal J between programmes.

The spot will run on public TV channels France 2 and France 3 during the broadcast of the world athletics championship, accompanied by a radio spot using the sound track of the TV film on music stations Europe 2 and Nostalgie.
The budget for the TV spot is 850,000 francs and for the radio spot is a million francs, a Canal J spokeswoman said.
She said the channel, France's first thematic channel launched in 1985 on a local cable network, wants the advertising campaign to help it to become better known.

Canal J is among the cable and satellite channels more often recognised by the public, according to studies, but even the best known of these, Eurosport, usually gets a recognition score under 30 percent.
Canal J has already run its TV spot on pay television station Canal Plus, which is a shareholder in Canal J, the spokeswoman said.

Canal J, which broadcasts during the day and early evening, had 1.87 million subscribers at the beginnining of July, of whom 1.33 million received it on cable networks and 540,000 via CanalSatellite, Canal Plus's satellite TV service which has carried Canal J since 1990, she said.
The channel aims to top two million subscribers by the end of this year, she said.

Canal J is owned 36.5 percent by Com-Dev Images, a unit of state-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC), 32.5 percent by Lyonnaise Communications, a unit of Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux, 19 percent by Canal Plus, six percent by magazine group Bayard Presse, 3.5 percent by Generale d'Images, a unit of Cie Generale des Eaux and 2.5 percent by magazine group Groupe Marie Claire.
